entities.summary: Microeconomics emerged in the 19th century as a distinct branch of economics, focusing on the behavior of individual households and firms in allocating limited resources. This led to significant changes in understanding and modeling economic systems, influencing economic policies and theories for decades to come. The development of microeconomics was heavily influenced by the works of Adam Smith, David Ricardo, and Carl Menger, among others. The key figures associated with this era include the emergence of the concept of opportunity cost and the development of the marginal analysis framework. The significance of microeconomics lies in its ability to provide insights into the decision-making processes of households and firms, which has far-reaching implications for understanding economic growth, inequality, and policy-making. As a result, microeconomics has played a crucial role in shaping modern economic thought and continues to be a fundamental area of study in economics today.
